headline: House votes to make daylight saving time permanent

sources.title: House passes bill to make daylight saving time permanent
House passes bill to make daylight saving time permanent
House passes Trump-backed bill that would make daylight saving time permanent

chunks.text: The US House of Representatives wants to {{do away with}} the twice-a-year clock changes. On Tuesday, [[lawmakers]] {{voted for}} a [[bill]] called the Sunshine Protection Act by 308 votes to 117. The plan would {{lock in}} [[permanent]] [[daylight saving time]] all across the country. Many [[supporters]] say the change is long overdue.

chunks.text: So what does 'changing the clocks' [[actually]] mean? In many countries, people turn their clocks forward by one hour in spring and back again in fall. This [[custom]] is called daylight saving time, and it helps people {{make use of}} the extra evening light in summer. The original goal was also to save energy. But twice each year, millions of people must {{get used to}} a new [[schedule]], and [[the switch]] can {{throw off}} their sleep for several days.

chunks.text: Many lawmakers were [[eager to]] {{press ahead}} with the plan, and the vote was [[bipartisan]]. They [[argue]] that lighter evenings could {{cut down on}} car accidents and give families more time outdoors after work. Several doctors add that a steady clock would be better for people. President Trump has {{come out}} [[in favor of]] the [[measure]] and has promised to sign it into law.

chunks.text: The bill now {{moves on}} to the [[Senate]], where its future is [[far from clear]]. Not every lawmaker {{goes along with}} the idea. [[Critics]] [[warn]] that winter mornings would stay dark for much longer, which could be risky for children who walk to school. Others recall that the country tried permanent daylight time back in 1973 but gave up on it within a year. For now, Americans must [[wait to see]] whether the Senate will {{take on}} the bill.

tf.s: The House voted for the Sunshine Protection Act by 308 votes to 117.
tf.why: The story says lawmakers voted for the bill by 308 votes to 117.

tf.s: The bill would lock in permanent standard time and make winter evenings darker.
tf.why: The bill would lock in permanent daylight saving time, not standard time, so evenings would be lighter.

tf.s: President Trump has come out against the plan and refused to sign it.
tf.why: Trump has actually come out in favor of the measure and promised to sign it into law.

tf.s: The bill now moves on to the Senate, where its future is unclear.
tf.why: The story says the bill moves on to the Senate, where its future is far from clear.

tf.s: Permanent daylight saving time would do away with the twice-a-year clock changes.
tf.why: The plan would do away with the switch, so people would no longer change their clocks each spring and fall.

tf.s: In 1973 the United States tried permanent daylight time, and every lawmaker went along with it.
tf.why: Not every lawmaker goes along with the idea today, and the 1973 attempt was ended within a year.
